articles.summary: In 2022, Tom Hanks launched Hanks for Our Troops, a nonprofit coffee brand dedicated to helping war veterans and their families. Discover how this initiative provides critical support and resources while promoting community service through coffee sales.
articles.body: In 2022, beloved star Tom Hanks, who is best known for his roles in ‘Toy Story’ and ‘Forrest Gump,' started a new kind of nonprofit project that has been helping military families for the past four years! Hanks officially launched his very own coffee brand under the nonprofit model, meaning none of the proceeds earned by the coffee will go to him; instead, they will be distributed to many military families across the nation.In 2022, Tom Hanks started his own coffee label to help war veteransInitially known as Hanx Coffee and now called Hanks for Our Troops, the coffee brand has a curated collection for coffee lovers. It offers ground coffee and single-serve pods in various roasts and flavours. Called “coffee with purpose," Hanks connected his brand with all kinds of veteran services that operate across America to provide funds and create awareness.On the official website of the coffee brand, the ‘story’ behind it all is written about how “At HANKS, we’re on a mission to create goods that do good. We honour the patriotism and service of our veterans and their families by giving all profits to organisations that will provide them with critical support and resources.” They also listed all of the organisations they work with and help by providing as much financial support as possible. These organisations work in different ways and sectors to help war veterans and their families, including employment, mental health resources, education, and assistance for military communities. People can order the coffee from the official website, though it is also available in-store at a popular chain.Hanks is not the only celebrity who has started similar initiatives to help the community around them. Paul Newman started his own salad dressing firm called ‘Newman's Own’ after he used to make it mainly for his family and neighbours, donating 100% of its profits to charity.About Tom Hanks and his philanthropic effortsOver the years, Tom Hanks has contributed continuously to all kinds of efforts and initiatives to give back to the community. He is also a campaign chair for the Hidden Heroes initiative, which raises awareness about officials who tend to injured and wounded war veterans at home and raises funds for their everyday resources. He also served as the official national campaign chairman for the World War II Memorial campaign in Washington, DC, and raised millions of dollars for the campaign. Other than that, Hanks has also invested in medical research and funding initiatives, with him and his wife, Rita Wilson, serving as Honorary Chairs for the Women’s Cancer Research Fund (WCRF). articles.summary: Veteran Bengali actress Mithu Mukherjee, who was a prominent screen presence in Bengali cinema during the 1970s and 1980s, has passed away at the age .
articles.body: Veteran Bengali actress Mithu Mukherjee, who was a prominent screen presence in Bengali cinema during the 1970s and 1980s, has passed away at the age of 71 in Mumbai, according to reports. The actress, known for films including Marjina Abdulla, Mouchak and Nishikanya, reportedly died at a private hospital on Sunday night after battling cancer for nearly a year. She had largely stayed away from the public eye in her later years.Mithu Mukherjee dies after prolonged illnessAccording to reports, Mithu Mukherjee breathed her last at a private hospital in Mumbai on Sunday night. The actress had reportedly been undergoing treatment for cancer for close to a year. Mithu had maintained a low profile in the later part of her life and largely remained away from the entertainment industry. Her death marks the passing of an actress who was closely associated with a significant period in Bengali cinema.Prosenjit Chatterjee and AICWA pay tributeFollowing news of her death, tributes began pouring in from the film fraternity. Bengali actor Prosenjit Chatterjee remembered Mithu in a post on X.“The news of Mithu Mukhopadhyay's passing is extremely heartbreaking. Her memory and her work will live on forever among us. With deepest respects,” he wrote.The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) also paid tribute to the veteran actress, remembering her contribution to Indian cinema.“Her contribution to Indian cinema and her memorable performances will continue to be remembered by audiences and the film fraternity. All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) pays its heartfelt tribute to the legendary actress. May her soul rest in peace,” the association said in its social media post.Mithu Mukherjee’s early life and Bengali film debutBorn in Kolkata in 1955, Mithu Mukherjee entered the Bengali film industry at the age of 17. She made her acting debut with Chitta Bose’s 'Shesh Parba' in 1972, opposite Shamit Bhanja. Her breakthrough came with Dinen Gupta’s 'Marjina Abdulla', in which she played the titular character. The film established her as a leading actress and helped her build a strong following among Bengali audiences.Working with Uttam Kumar, Soumitra Chattopadhyay and Ranjit MullickDuring her career, Mithu Mukherjee shared screen space with several leading actors of Bengali cinema, including Uttam Kumar, Soumitra Chattopadhyay and Ranjit Mullick. Her notable Bengali films include 'Nishikanya', 'Mouchak', 'Kabi', 'Hotel Snow Fox', 'Pratima', 'Bandhan' and 'Prarthana'. Her performances during this period established her as a familiar face in Bengali films of the era.Mithu Mukherjee’s Hindi film careerMithu also ventured into Hindi cinema in 1976 with Dulal Guha’s 'Khaan Dost'. She subsequently appeared in films including Basu Chatterjee’s 'Safed Jhoot', 'Dillagi' and 'Do Ladke Dono Kadke'. Although her career was predominantly associated with Bengali cinema, her Hindi film appearances brought her work to a wider audience.Her final film and life away from the spotlightAfter appearing in 'Dujane' in the 1980s, Mithu Mukherjee took an extended break from acting. She returned to the screen in 1990 with Chandra Barot’s 'Ashrita', which became her final film appearance. articles.title: Le preguntan a Sarah Santaolalla por su entrevista preferida para La Séptima y no duda en responder: "Me parece que Mbappé lo ha hecho bien con lo de la camiseta"
articles.standfirst: La presentadora de la nueva cadena responde a una serie de preguntas en la promoción del canal
articles.summary: La presentadora de la nueva cadena responde a una serie de preguntas en la promoción del canal
articles.body: El próximo 5 de noviembre llega a todas las pantallas la nueva cadena de televisión La Séptima. Hasta que llegue la fecha, el medio de comunicación se ha encargado, a través de sus redes sociales, de desvelar sus nuevas caras. El proyecto, impulsado por José Miguel Contreras, contará con caras conocidas de la televisión. Entre ellas, Sarah Santaolalla. La cadena comunicó el pasado 31 de agosto que la periodista estará al frente de su propio programa, dando así un importante salto en su carrera después de estar varios años como colaboradora y tertuliana en varios espacios de actualidad. Hasta que llegue el día de su estreno, La Séptima ha compartido en sus redes sociales un vídeo en el que le lanzan preguntas a la presentadora para conocerla más. En el vídeo aparece junto al humorista y también una de las incorporaciones de la cadena, Quequé. A ambos le preguntan a quién les gustaría entrevistar. Mientras que el cómico, con humor responde: “A uno de derecha, derecha como Felipe Gónzalez”, Santaolalla contesta: “A un Mbappé”. La periodista confiesa en su respuesta que cree que el jugador del Real Madrid “lo ha hecho muy bien con lo de la camiseta”. Haciendo así alusión a la polémica del francés al no ponerse por completo la camiseta de apoyo a Ceuta antes del partido entre el Elche y el Real Madrid. “Debemos ser empáticos con los ciudadanos de Ceuta y también con los que han muerto en el mar”, añade. Por eso le gustaría que el invitado en su programa de La Séptima fuera Kilian Mbappé. A la pregunta de si podría adelantar algo de su programa, la presentadora ha sido contundente: “Aquí no vais a ver a negacionistas, ni terraplanistas, ni nazis, ni a un científico frente a un tipo que dice que nos fumigan, ni esos debates en los que sientan por igual y equiparan a un violador y a su víctima, a un maltratador y a su víctima. Eso de nazis sí, nazis, no. No, No. Vamos a ser plurales, pero no equidistantes”, confiesa.

articles.title: Presley Gerber dies at 27. What Cindy Crawford's model son said about recovery, medication and feeling 'misunderstood.'
articles.summary: Gerber, the son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber, had spoken publicly about his mental health and experiences with addiction.
articles.body:
Presley Gerber, a model and the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, died Sunday. He was 27.

Gerber died at a rehabilitation facility, according to online records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. A cause of death was not listed.

"The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time," said Allie Jenkins, a representative for Crawford and Rande Gerber.

Gerber was the older brother of model and actor Kaia Gerber. He was signed by IMG Models at age 15 and modeled for brands including Dolce & Gabbana, Moschino, Burberry, Tommy Hilfiger and Ralph Lauren.

He had previously spoken about his mental health and experiences with addiction. In 2018, he was arrested on a charge of DUI and sentenced to three years' probation.

In 2020, Gerber had the word "misunderstood" tattooed on his right cheek. "It says misunderstood, because that's how I felt my entire life," he said in a livestreamed Instagram video. The tattoo appeared to have been removed the following year.

"Having struggled with mental health, depression and some other things that come along with that, I think that whether I help one person or a hundred people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that's all I need to do," he told the Studio 22 podcast in 2023.

He added, "[Mental health] is an issue. It is such a big part of my life. It's a 24/7 job, and there's so much to it. That's really what I want to do: help people. Whether you're depressed, you're struggling with something that is having a negative effect on your body. I mean, it could be anything, and there's no judgment."

In an Instagram video posted in December 2025, Gerber said he wanted clearer guidance from his doctors. "Every psychiatrist I've had, and I've had 15, are just like, 'Well, here's 20 medications and take this if you feel like this,'" he said. "And I'm like, 'No, don't give me that much leeway.' I need some direction."

In the same video, he said he had stopped drinking. "That is no longer serving me," he said.

In one of his final Instagram posts , shared in March, Gerber posted footage from Mexico taken before undergoing what he called an "ibogaine flood dose." Ibogaine, a psychoactive drug derived from the root of an African shrub, is not approved for medical use in the U.S. He wrote, "I faced what I had been running from, and somewhere in all of it, I started finding my way back to myself."

In an interview with Vogue published last month, Kaia reflected on her brother's history with addiction. She said, "When something like that happens in a family, it kind of levels everyone. I think that's also why I started to self-​identify as the easy one and never wanted to ask for help. Because it felt like too much to have two children who were needing."

Gerber's family has yet to comment beyond their representative's statement requesting privacy.

In an Instagram Stories post, Gerber's friend Paris Hilton said she was "completely heartbroken." She added, "Presley, you were such a beautiful soul. So sweet, sensitive, kind and genuine. I cared about you so much, and I'm going to miss you more than words can say."

If you or someone you know is struggling with mental health challenges, emotional distress, substance use problems, or just needs to talk, call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org 24/7. Alternatively, contact the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) National Helpline on 1-800-662-HELP (4357) or text your ZIP code to HELP4U (435748).
